$comment: W-1 warranty spec companion, 2026-10-20. Firebase-parity holders derived READ-ONLY from functions/src/access/{permissionCatalog,compatibilityRoles,governedBusinessRoles}.ts at main b3d09dc3 (scratch copy in the lane scratchpad; nothing written to a role, a grant, a database or a fixture; nothing deleted). No migration is proposed by this file. The parity set for any NEW warranty key is empty.
decision: Brief 2026-10-20: derive Firebase-parity holders A7-style. Grants not in exact Firebase parity are a STOP. None is authorized by this file.

baseline.firebaseSource: main b3d09dc3 functions/src/access/{permissionCatalog.ts, compatibilityRoles.ts, governedBusinessRoles.ts} and firestore.rules:1334-1363,1468-1508
baseline.eosSource: NOT READ from any environment. EOS holders are Administration data in eos_policy.role_capabilities; the repository seed (functions/src/adminPolicy/equipmentActivationDelta.ts, Controller ruling 2026-10-01 OD-2/OD-3) is the ruled baseline, not the live table.

newKeySearch.note: No Firebase permission key names warranty. The hidden service/warranty navigation item records 'No warranty domain, no capability, no backend' (navConfig.js:889). Firebase gated equipment by Firestore Rules (isAdminOrDispatcher), not by a permission key.

firebaseRulesAuthority.note: Source: firestore.rules match /equipment/{equipmentId}. installedDate and warrantyExpiresDate are in equipmentEditableKeys() and are plain optional strings. There is no Firebase warranty computation, status or judgment anywhere.

equipment.record.read.firebaseNote: EOS-native key; Firebase equivalent is Rules isAdminOrDispatcher (read).
equipment.record.read.use: see the derived warranty status on the Equipment record and register; unchanged

equipment.record.manage.firebaseNote: EOS-native key; Firebase equivalent is Rules isAdminOrDispatcher (create, update). EOS narrowed this on purpose (2026-10-01 OD-3).
equipment.record.manage.use: record, correct or end a coverage by hand; edit installed_on and warranty_expires_on as today

workOrder.record.read.firebaseNote: EOS-native key; Firebase gates Work Order reads by Rules.
workOrder.record.read.eosHoldersRuled: per the Work Order read decision (assigned Employee for a Technician)
workOrder.record.read.use: see the derived warranty status on a Work Order the caller may already read

equipment.model.manage.use: maintain the warranty terms catalog (terms keyed by manufacturer and model)

equipment.install.use: the install visit that supplies the start fact; unchanged

report.equipment.field.dates.read.use: report on installedDate and warrantyExpiresDate (the catalog `dates` field group)

excluded.reason: Proposed only as OD-14 option B. Firebase never held a warranty key, so the parity set is empty and every holder would be a non-parity grant: a STOP. The recommended option (OD-14 A) reuses existing keys and needs no grant.
Firebase Rules let Dispatcher edit both dates; EOS narrowed it on purpose on 2026-10-01 (OD-3). Restoring it is a policy ruling on a role the Owner narrowed, not part of W-1 (OD-14 C).

notes: Declaring or reusing a capability grants nothing; Administration data decides who holds it.
The recommended design adds no read capability: warranty status is a derived projection shown through surfaces whose gates already exist.

EOS read reach is wider than Firebase's (Technician through the Work Order, Salesperson through a channel scope, the operational roles). That is an existing Owner ruling and is neither widened nor narrowed here.
